senses.definition: The condition of being fit, suitable or appropriate.

quotes.text: Having introduced my two characters separately, let me present them together. Why not? He, young, wealthy, honorable; she also young, also intelligent — why not bring them together? There is an eternal fitness in all things, and nothing more so than in the case of man and woman.
quotes.reference: 1861, E. J. Guerin, Mountain Charley, page 5:

quotes.text: That's chiefly why they're coming; I want you to meet them here and then tell me frankly what you think of their fitness for whatever we decide on doing.
quotes.reference: 1934, Ernest Bramah, The Bravo of London:

senses.definition: The cultivation of an attractive and/or healthy physique.

quotes.text: Carroll has been edging slowly towards full fitness after his expensive arrival from Newcastle United and his partnership with £23m Luis Suarez showed rich promise as Liverpool controlled affairs from start to finish.
quotes.reference: 2011 April 11, Phil McNulty, “Liverpool 3 - 0 Man City”, in BBC Sport:

senses.definition: (evolutionary theory) An organism's or species' degree of success in finding a mate and producing offspring.
(UK, slang) The condition of being attractive, fanciable or beautiful.
